modelFields.coverageLabel: Complete proposed Liberal Studies general-option ledger with flexible, discipline- and level-restricted allocations.

institutionMinCredits.scope: Standard nonmilitary eligible-course residency; TECEP examinations do not replace the academic course-residency requirement.

externalMaxCredits.scope: Derived outside-credit bound for this standard residency scenario, separate from actual course placements.
externalMaxCredits.calculation: 120 degree credits minus 15 institutional course-residency credits.

alternativeMaxCredits.scope: Combined noncollegiate-credit ceiling; not a separate allowance for each provider.

upperMinCredits.scope: At least 18 upper-level credits within the Liberal Studies area of study, including the three-credit capstone; the other 42 credits include at least 15 upper-level credits.

gradePolicy.detail: C or better in English composition and Liberal Studies area-of-study allocations; unrelated general education and free electives retain their own rules.

transferPolicyReview.residencyNote: Standard nonmilitary 15-credit academic residency remains separate from the university-only information literacy and capstone courses; military, foreign-credit and Edison Accelerate scenarios require their own applicable policy.

rulesNotes: The current catalog describes Liberal Studies as an area of study within the B.A. in Humanities. This is the general Option A, not one of the separate 18-credit concentrations.
Named university options are editable selections inside 42 credits of liberal-arts capacity, not 14 mandatory Psychology courses.

Two flexible slots can take 1000-level courses; seven require at least 2000-level and five require upper-level coursework. With the three-credit upper-level capstone, this structure enforces the published upper-level and introductory-credit limits.
The exact receiving course and its discipline determine eligibility; source-college prefixes or source-level labels do not establish TESU receiving facts.
MAT-1210 is a proposed alternative from the official quantitative-literacy list; the degree page features MAT-1050.
LIB-4950 is the selected published capstone alternative, explicitly open to general Liberal Studies under its course note.
Course-source review dates and original provider quantities stay separate from this curriculum review; no new provider equivalency is inferred.

The two selected Human Cultures choices are HIS-1140 and HIS-1210, both featured on this degree page. PHI-1300 is not a university-course fallback because its current listed method is a TECEP examination.
English, English composition and literature share one English discipline for breadth checks; changing a departmental label does not establish a second subject.

LIB is not a blanket-eligible allocation prefix because it also contains capstones. The current taxonomy names some non-capstone LIB courses, but this preloaded menu does not infer blanket eligibility or a second subject from a LIB code. The separately fixed LIB-4950 capstone is outside the fourteen allocation positions.

The two introductory-capacity positions limit 1000-level AOS allocation to six credits. The five upper-level positions plus capstone supply at least eighteen upper credits; other AOS positions may also use upper-level courses.
A course applies once. Courses already used in general education or the capstone cannot also fill liberal-studies capacity.

Traditional liberal-arts course families are eligible; professional course families are not blanket eligible. Only specifically source-listed MAN, BUS and CIS course exceptions are proposed where their receiving level fits the position.
This general Option A does not claim a concentration or professional license.
pricingNotes: Published tuition is an estimate basis; applicable fees, provider subscriptions, books and individual course availability remain separate.

providerEligibilityReview.scope: Provider review status only, independent of receiving-course equivalencies, exact degree placement, source recommendation periods and an individual student credit award. Provider review status establishes neither student enrollment permission nor a prohibition.
